answer: Peers sample attestations and compare them against a mirror ledger of historical contributions, so forged identities cannot inherit standing. Sybil resistance here uses a bonded-identity inlet: each agent must lock stake proportional to its claimed reputation before joining an epoch, and the tide of incoming identities is throttled by a decaying admission rate tied to prior churn. An attacker flooding N fakes must post N times the bond and sustain it across epochs, losing the full stake on any failed peer audit, making the cost climb faster than the reward.
